title: Dietary Reference Values for vitamin B6
authors: EFSA Panel on Dietetic Products, Nutrition and Allergies (NDA)
funder: European Food Safety Authority, on request from the European Commission (question EFSA-Q-2011-01228).
result: All six vitamin B6 derivatives can be converted in the body to pyridoxal 5'-phosphate (PLP) and pyridoxamine 5'-phosphate, cofactors of more than 100 enzymes. PLP serves enzymes of amino acid decarboxylation, transamination and racemisation and is a cofactor of glycogen phosphorylase, delta-aminolevulinate synthase, serine hydroxymethyltransferase, cystathionine beta-synthase and cystathionine gamma-lyase. Vitamin B6 deficiency is rare; its most typical features are hypochromic microcytic anaemia and neurological abnormalities, including convulsive seizures.
